title: Two- and three-day NOAA electron forecasts lost to persistence in 57 issue dates in September to November 2026
abstract: We tested NOAA SWPC daily electron fluence forecasts at three leads in a fixed public table. On 57 common issue dates, two- and three-day mean squared log errors were 4.18 and 2.79 times persistence errors. Seven-day block intervals for paired excess error were above zero; one-day performance was uncertain. Small pooled log biases hid opposite errors. After solar wind speeds of at least 450 km/s, geometric forecast-to-observation ratios were 10.72 and 12.47 at the longer leads; below that speed they were 0.44 and 0.45. This split was post hoc. A simple level replacement kept negative skill, so it did not support a common-level-only remedy. The study adds a conditional error audit, not the first REFM verification. It uses sixty observed days from September to November 2026, selected after signs of poor performance. Few independent episodes, a rolling source table, lack of independent GOES truth and no internal model replay limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and a scalar audit support reproduction.

display.caption: Public electron fluence forecasts and observed values, common-sample errors, speed-dependent bias and seven-day excess errors. Future forecasts in the time series are not scored.
